prompt: This EMCDDA–Europol Joint Report on MDPV is cited for the items below. Report each exactly as printed, and say 'not found' for any that is absent: (a) the total quantities seized across the EU (kilograms of powder, number of tablets, number of cases); (b) the date up to which information was collected; (c) when the samples from Irish head shops were analysed; (d) the years given for the Bulgarian seizures of Doves Red, Ivory Wave, Mojo, Flower Magic Powder and Load, and for the Slovak products Long Play, Beep Beep, Speed Way, Popeyes Sniff and LP, and how these product names are capitalised. Do not quote any passage longer than 15 words.
answer:
**(a) Total quantities seized across the EU:** The report gives no combined EU total. For powder, it cites "more than 4 500 individual cases" amounting to "an excess of 200 kg." For tablets or capsules, it cites "over 500 cases" containing "approximately 30 000 tablets in total."

**(b) Date up to which information was collected:** Collection was "largely concluded by 18 November 2013." Some countries sent clarifications up to four weeks after that date.

**(c) Analysis of Irish head shop samples:** March 2010 (Annex 1).

**(d) Bulgarian and Slovak product years and capitalisation:**

- **Bulgaria:** The report gives a period for the 12 customs seizures, July 2010 to March 2012, but no year specific to any product. "DOVES RED" has no product-specific year, so the year is not found. "IVORY WAVE," "MOJO," "FLOWER MAGIC POWDER" and "LOAD" have no years given, so those are not found. The report prints all five names in uppercase.
- **Slovakia:** No years are given for "Long Play," "Beep Beep," "Speed Way," "Popeyes Sniff" or "LP," so all are not found. The report prints them in title case, with "LP" as an abbreviation.
